extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, complainants, media lawyers, and members of the public interested in press standards
extracted.subtask_description: An archive page listing Independent Press Standards Organisation complaints and decisions, showing the Editors’ Code clauses alleged to be breached, the complaint summaries, published dates, outcomes, and any sanctions or mediation summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause 1 (Accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequently cited in complaints alleging factual errors or misleading headlines; outcomes shown on the page include both 'No breach - after investigation' and 'Breach - sanction: publication of correction', indicating that investigations evaluate whether published material was factually accurate and whether correction is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause 2 (Privacy)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in complaints alleging unjustified intrusion into individuals' private lives; appears alongside other clauses (e.g. Accuracy) in multi-issue complaints. Outcomes on the page include both breach and no-breach findings depending on investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause 3 (Harassment)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited where complainants allege harassment by a publication; appears in combination with privacy and discrimination complaints in at least one listed case, implying evaluation of whether conduct amounted to harassment under the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause 4 (Intrusion into grief or shock)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoked in complaints concerning coverage that may intrude on grieving individuals; included as an alleged breach in at least one case, with the outcome recorded (breach in the listed example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause 5 (Reporting suicide)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced where reporting may touch on suicide-related material; listed among code provisions in at least one complaint entry, indicating evaluation against this specific reporting standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause 9 (Reporting of crime)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in complaints alleging problems with how crime was reported; one listed outcome is 'No breach - after investigation', showing the Committee assesses whether reporting complied with the clause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clause 12 (Discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in complaints alleging discriminatory content or treatment; appears in a multi-clause complaint on the page, indicating the Code's discrimination standard is applied in investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome categories (Breach / No breach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcome labels shown include 'No breach - after investigation' and 'Breach - sanction: ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes record whether the Complaints Committee found a breach of the Editors’ Code following investigation, and when a breach is found the page records the sanction type (examples shown: 'publication of correction', 'action as offered by publication'). The archive ties outcomes to specific code provisions for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions recorded (publication of correction; action as offered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanction types shown include 'publication of correction' and 'action as offered by publication'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When breaches are found the archive records the remedial step imposed or accepted; examples on the page show publication of corrections and publication-proposed actions as sanctions or remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication policy for rulings and mediated summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: All rulings made by the Complaints Committee are published in full, along with summaries of all complaints which have been resolved via mediation by IPSO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The archive is intended to provide transparency: full rulings and mediation summaries are published with complaint summaries, dates, code provisions cited, and outcomes. This implies a standard of public disclosure and recordkeeping for complaints handling.
